sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording of a line ("full of the Spirit and ___"). Wisdom, courage and strength are all plausible, and nothing earlier lets a baker reason out which one the text uses.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess which name (Moses, Abraham or David) completes the accusers' quoted line. No earlier card in the passage mentions Moses, so a baker can only guess, not reason it out.
sonnet.rule: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The joke repeats the punchline shape of card 3: "I can't even get [things] to agree" echoes "I could never even get the dead batteries... to come to a meeting." Both are the same "I can't even get X to Y" shape in one lesson.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
